overview:
Minnesota's 4th District leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of 18 points, and Betty McCollum has held the seat for more than two decades. She enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.5 million and holding over $500,000 on hand, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised roughly $65,000. No outside groups are spending against McCollum, and prediction markets give her roughly a 96 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Those factors all point the same way: a comfortable Democratic win in a reliably blue seat. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin, which recent district history suggests should land in the low-to-mid twenties.
